title: SMILE: A Structured Multi-Agent Clinical Reasoning for Liver Ultrasound Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2611.02581v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automated liver ultrasound report generation improves the diagnosis of liver diseases by producing clinically structured descriptions of anatomical and disease-related findings. However, current generative vision-language models (VLMs) often rely on a single reasoning pathway that maps ultrasound appearance directly to textual descriptions. In addition to the inherent vision-language modality gap, this design is limited for liver ultrasound because disease interpretation is constrained by subtle visual evidence, heterogeneous disease patterns, and limited paired supervision. translated_title: SMILE：一种用于肝脏超声理解的结构化多智能体临床推理框架
translated_abstract: 自动化的肝脏超声报告生成通过生成具有临床结构化格式的解剖结构与疾病相关发现的描述，有助于改善肝脏疾病的诊断。然而，当前的生成式视觉-语言模型（VLMs）通常依赖单一的推理路径，将超声图像表现直接映射为文本描述。除了视觉与语言模态之间固有的差异外，这种设计在肝脏超声任务中存在局限，因为疾病解读受到细微视觉证据、异质性疾病模式以及有限配对监督数据的制约。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了SMILE，一个结构化多智能体临床推理框架，它利用多个互补的专科智能体来解读超声图像，并通过裁判引导的共识机制整合各智能体的输出。我们的方法采用三个专门化智能体：用于形态学描述的图像解读智能体，……
tldr: 该论文提出SMILE框架，通过多个互补的专科智能体解读肝脏超声图像，并利用裁判引导的共识机制整合结果，从而克服单一推理路径的局限，提升肝脏超声报告生成的质量。
en_tdlr: SMILE is a structured multi-agent clinical reasoning framework that employs complementary specialist agents and a judge-guided consensus mechanism to overcome single-pathway limitations and improve liver ultrasound report generation.
